title: Leviticus 7: Christ Our Peace Offering
body:
Read the chapter → [Leviticus 7](/bible/leviticus/7)

**[Leviticus 7:1-7](/bible/leviticus/7#v1)**

> <sup>[1](/bible/leviticus/7#v1)</sup> Likewise this is the law of the trespass offering: it is most holy.
>
> <sup>[2](/bible/leviticus/7#v2)</sup> In the place where they kill the burnt offering shall they kill the trespass offering: and the blood thereof shall he sprinkle round about upon the altar.
>
> <sup>[3](/bible/leviticus/7#v3)</sup> And he shall offer of it all the fat thereof; the rump, and the fat that covereth the inwards,
>
> <sup>[4](/bible/leviticus/7#v4)</sup> And the two kidneys, and the fat that is on them, which is by the flanks, and the caul that is above the liver, with the kidneys, it shall he take away:
>
> <sup>[5](/bible/leviticus/7#v5)</sup> And the priest shall burn them upon the altar for an offering made by fire unto the Lord: it is a trespass offering.
>
> <sup>[6](/bible/leviticus/7#v6)</sup> Every male among the priests shall eat thereof: it shall be eaten in the holy place: it is most holy.
>
> <sup>[7](/bible/leviticus/7#v7)</sup> As the sin offering is, so is the trespass offering: there is one law for them: the priest that maketh atonement therewith shall have it.

- Likewise this is the law of the trespass offering: it is most holy. The fat, the rump, the fat that covers the inwards, the kidneys, and the caul above the liver, basically the guts, were burnt upon the altar, and as the sin offering is, so is the trespass offering; there is one law for them.
- Paul was a master of the law, and trespass in his letters goes back to this law: you hath he quickened, who were dead in trespasses and sins, when in time past we walked according to the course of this world, according to the prince of the power of the air, which is Satan.
- By grace ye are saved means all of us deserve death for our sins, but through Christ we have grace and are saved from the destruction to come, if we endure to the end keeping the commandments.

  Precepts:
  - **[Ephesians 2:1-5](/bible/ephesians/2#v1)**
    > <sup>[1](/bible/ephesians/2#v1)</sup> And you hath he quickened, who were dead in trespasses and sins;
    >
    > <sup>[2](/bible/ephesians/2#v2)</sup> Wherein in time past ye walked according to the course of this world, according to the prince of the power of the air, the spirit that now worketh in the children of disobedience:
    >
    > <sup>[3](/bible/ephesians/2#v3)</sup> Among whom also we all had our conversation in times past in the lusts of our flesh, fulfilling the desires of the flesh and of the mind; and were by nature the children of wrath, even as others.
    >
    > <sup>[4](/bible/ephesians/2#v4)</sup> But God, who is rich in mercy, for his great love wherewith he loved us,
    >
    > <sup>[5](/bible/ephesians/2#v5)</sup> Even when we were dead in sins, hath quickened us together with Christ, (by grace ye are saved;)

    You hath he quickened, who were dead in trespasses and sins; God, who is rich in mercy, even when we were dead in sins, hath quickened us together with Christ; by grace ye are saved.
  - **[Romans 6:23](/bible/romans/6#v23)**
    > <sup>[23](/bible/romans/6#v23)</sup> For the wages of sin is death; but the gift of God is eternal life through Jesus Christ our Lord.

    The wages of sin is death, but the gift of God is eternal life through Jesus Christ; that is the grace, that we are not killed for our sins.

**[Leviticus 7:11-18](/bible/leviticus/7#v11)**

> <sup>[11](/bible/leviticus/7#v11)</sup> And this is the law of the sacrifice of peace offerings, which he shall offer unto the Lord.
>
> <sup>[12](/bible/leviticus/7#v12)</sup> If he offer it for a thanksgiving, then he shall offer with the sacrifice of thanksgiving unleavened cakes mingled with oil, and unleavened wafers anointed with oil, and cakes mingled with oil, of fine flour, fried.
>
> <sup>[13](/bible/leviticus/7#v13)</sup> Besides the cakes, he shall offer for his offering leavened bread with the sacrifice of thanksgiving of his peace offerings.
>
> <sup>[14](/bible/leviticus/7#v14)</sup> And of it he shall offer one out of the whole oblation for an heave offering unto the Lord, and it shall be the priest’s that sprinkleth the blood of the peace offerings.
>
> <sup>[15](/bible/leviticus/7#v15)</sup> And the flesh of the sacrifice of his peace offerings for thanksgiving shall be eaten the same day that it is offered; he shall not leave any of it until the morning.
>
> <sup>[16](/bible/leviticus/7#v16)</sup> But if the sacrifice of his offering be a vow, or a voluntary offering, it shall be eaten the same day that he offereth his sacrifice: and on the morrow also the remainder of it shall be eaten:
>
> <sup>[17](/bible/leviticus/7#v17)</sup> But the remainder of the flesh of the sacrifice on the third day shall be burnt with fire.
>
> <sup>[18](/bible/leviticus/7#v18)</sup> And if any of the flesh of the sacrifice of his peace offerings be eaten at all on the third day, it shall not be accepted, neither shall it be imputed unto him that offereth it: it shall be an abomination, and the soul that eateth of it shall bear his iniquity.

- This is the law of the sacrifice of peace offerings. If it was offered for a thanksgiving, the flesh was eaten the same day it was offered; none was left until the morning.
- If the sacrifice was a vow or a voluntary offering, it was eaten the same day and the remainder on the morrow also; that is the difference between the two. But flesh remaining on the third day was burnt with fire, and if any was eaten on the third day it was an abomination, and the offering was not accepted.

**[Leviticus 7:19-21](/bible/leviticus/7#v19)**

> <sup>[19](/bible/leviticus/7#v19)</sup> And the flesh that toucheth any unclean thing shall not be eaten; it shall be burnt with fire: and as for the flesh, all that be clean shall eat thereof.
>
> <sup>[20](/bible/leviticus/7#v20)</sup> But the soul that eateth of the flesh of the sacrifice of peace offerings, that pertain unto the Lord, having his uncleanness upon him, even that soul shall be cut off from his people.
>
> <sup>[21](/bible/leviticus/7#v21)</sup> Moreover the soul that shall touch any unclean thing, as the uncleanness of man, or any unclean beast, or any abominable unclean thing, and eat of the flesh of the sacrifice of peace offerings, which pertain unto the Lord, even that soul shall be cut off from his people.

- The flesh that touched any unclean thing was not eaten but burnt with fire, and the soul that ate of the peace offerings having his uncleanness upon him was cut off from his people. An unclean man coming into the tabernacle to sacrifice or a priest eating unclean was facing death before the Lord.
- All the touching of unclean and defiled things pertains to sacrifice: the point of the uncleanness laws was to separate the children of Israel from their uncleanness, that they die not when they defile the tabernacle. There is no more sacrifice, so those defilement laws do not apply today; a brother can brush his hair with a brush of boar bristles, because that law was about coming in to sacrifice.

  Precepts:
  - **[Leviticus 15:31](/bible/leviticus/15#v31)**
    > <sup>[31](/bible/leviticus/15#v31)</sup> Thus shall ye separate the children of Israel from their uncleanness; that they die not in their uncleanness, when they defile my tabernacle that is among them.

    Thus shall ye separate the children of Israel from their uncleanness, that they die not, when they defile my tabernacle; the uncleanness laws guarded the sacrifice.

**[Leviticus 7:22-27](/bible/leviticus/7#v22)**

> <sup>[22](/bible/leviticus/7#v22)</sup> And the Lord spake unto Moses, saying,
>
> <sup>[23](/bible/leviticus/7#v23)</sup> Speak unto the children of Israel, saying, Ye shall eat no manner of fat, of ox, or of sheep, or of goat.
>
> <sup>[24](/bible/leviticus/7#v24)</sup> And the fat of the beast that dieth of itself, and the fat of that which is torn with beasts, may be used in any other use: but ye shall in no wise eat of it.
>
> <sup>[25](/bible/leviticus/7#v25)</sup> For whosoever eateth the fat of the beast, of which men offer an offering made by fire unto the Lord, even the soul that eateth it shall be cut off from his people.
>
> <sup>[26](/bible/leviticus/7#v26)</sup> Moreover ye shall eat no manner of blood, whether it be of fowl or of beast, in any of your dwellings.
>
> <sup>[27](/bible/leviticus/7#v27)</sup> Whatsoever soul it be that eateth any manner of blood, even that soul shall be cut off from his people.

- Ye shall eat no manner of fat, of ox, or of sheep, or of goat: this pertained to the sacrifices. The fat upon the sacrifices was either burnt completely or put to other uses; there is no sin in eating fat off an animal now, because what it pertained to was the sacrifice.
- One of those other uses was soap: Israel took the fat and made soap with it. Jeremiah shows it, though thou wash thee with nitre, and take thee much soap; Israel had soap way back then and did not live filthy, and when the Moors ruled in Europe they introduced soap to Esau again.
- But blood was different: no manner of blood, of fowl or of beast, in any of your dwellings, whether sacrificing or not. The soul that eats any manner of blood shall be cut off; cook the food well done, not rare, and that stands to this day.

  Precepts:
  - **[Jeremiah 2:22](/bible/jeremiah/2#v22)**
    > <sup>[22](/bible/jeremiah/2#v22)</sup> For though thou wash thee with nitre, and take thee much soap, yet thine iniquity is marked before me, saith the Lord God.

    Though thou wash thee with nitre, and take thee much soap, yet thine iniquity is marked before me; soap was known in Israel of old, made from the fat.

**[Leviticus 7:28-34](/bible/leviticus/7#v28)**

> <sup>[28](/bible/leviticus/7#v28)</sup> And the Lord spake unto Moses, saying,
>
> <sup>[29](/bible/leviticus/7#v29)</sup> Speak unto the children of Israel, saying, He that offereth the sacrifice of his peace offerings unto the Lord shall bring his oblation unto the Lord of the sacrifice of his peace offerings.
>
> <sup>[30](/bible/leviticus/7#v30)</sup> His own hands shall bring the offerings of the Lord made by fire, the fat with the breast, it shall he bring, that the breast may be waved for a wave offering before the Lord.
>
> <sup>[31](/bible/leviticus/7#v31)</sup> And the priest shall burn the fat upon the altar: but the breast shall be Aaron’s and his sons’.
>
> <sup>[32](/bible/leviticus/7#v32)</sup> And the right shoulder shall ye give unto the priest for an heave offering of the sacrifices of your peace offerings.
>
> <sup>[33](/bible/leviticus/7#v33)</sup> He among the sons of Aaron, that offereth the blood of the peace offerings, and the fat, shall have the right shoulder for his part.
>
> <sup>[34](/bible/leviticus/7#v34)</sup> For the wave breast and the heave shoulder have I taken of the children of Israel from off the sacrifices of their peace offerings, and have given them unto Aaron the priest and unto his sons by a statute for ever from among the children of Israel.

- He that offered his peace offerings brought the oblation with his own hands: the fat with the breast, that the breast may be waved for a wave offering before the LORD. The wave offering was heaved up and waved before the Lord as a sign, proof of what he had brought.
- The wave breast and the heave shoulder were given to Aaron the priest and his sons by a statute for ever; this is how the priests ate from the peace offerings. [Leviticus 10](/bible/leviticus/10) returns to these portions, the wave breast and heave shoulder given to Aaron and his sons and daughters; chapters 6 through 10 explain the offerings.

  Precepts:
  - **[Exodus 29:27](/bible/exodus/29#v27)**
    > <sup>[27](/bible/exodus/29#v27)</sup> And thou shalt sanctify the breast of the wave offering, and the shoulder of the heave offering, which is waved, and which is heaved up, of the ram of the consecration, even of that which is for Aaron, and of that which is for his sons:

    Sanctify the breast of the wave offering, and the shoulder of the heave offering, which is waved, and which is heaved up; the offering was lifted and waved before the Lord.

**[Leviticus 7:35-38](/bible/leviticus/7#v35)**

> <sup>[35](/bible/leviticus/7#v35)</sup> This is the portion of the anointing of Aaron, and of the anointing of his sons, out of the offerings of the Lord made by fire, in the day when he presented them to minister unto the Lord in the priest’s office;
>
> <sup>[36](/bible/leviticus/7#v36)</sup> Which the Lord commanded to be given them of the children of Israel, in the day that he anointed them, by a statute for ever throughout their generations.
>
> <sup>[37](/bible/leviticus/7#v37)</sup> This is the law of the burnt offering, of the meat offering, and of the sin offering, and of the trespass offering, and of the consecrations, and of the sacrifice of the peace offerings;
>
> <sup>[38](/bible/leviticus/7#v38)</sup> Which the Lord commanded Moses in mount Sinai, in the day that he commanded the children of Israel to offer their oblations unto the Lord, in the wilderness of Sinai.

- Verse 37 lists all the different offerings in one place: the burnt offering, the meat offering, the sin offering, the trespass offering, the consecrations, and the sacrifice of the peace offerings, which the LORD commanded Moses in mount Sinai.
- Christ is our peace, our peace offering between us and the Most High. He abolished in his flesh the enmity, even the law of commandments contained in ordinances; the ordinances are the law of sacrifice, sprinkle the blood seven times, a lamb without blemish, eaten before the third day, carried without the camp, burnt to ashes with the garments changed.
- Let no man therefore judge you in meat or in drink: add the word offering, the meat offering and drink offering we just read in Leviticus. No man can condemn you because you are not sacrificing animals any more, or for how you observe a holyday, new moon, or sabbath pertaining to sacrifice, for those are a shadow of things to come, but the body is of Christ.
- The law of sacrifice was contrary to us because those sacrifices offered year by year continually could never make the comers thereunto perfect. It was a scapegoat so the law would not have to kill us; the Most High has been extending grace since Adam, for he had every right to kill Adam and Eve, and instead extended grace through the animal sacrifice. If the law of sacrifice still stood, there would be no sacrifice for worshipping other gods, and we would be done as a people; it was taken out of the way so Israel could come back to God.

  Precepts:
  - **[Ephesians 2:13-16](/bible/ephesians/2#v13)**
    > <sup>[13](/bible/ephesians/2#v13)</sup> But now in Christ Jesus ye who sometimes were far off are made nigh by the blood of Christ.
    >
    > <sup>[14](/bible/ephesians/2#v14)</sup> For he is our peace, who hath made both one, and hath broken down the middle wall of partition between us;
    >
    > <sup>[15](/bible/ephesians/2#v15)</sup> Having abolished in his flesh the enmity, even the law of commandments contained in ordinances; for to make in himself of twain one new man, so making peace;
    >
    > <sup>[16](/bible/ephesians/2#v16)</sup> And that he might reconcile both unto God in one body by the cross, having slain the enmity thereby:

    Ye who sometimes were far off are made nigh by the blood of Christ: for he is our peace, who hath abolished in his flesh the law of commandments contained in ordinances, and reconciled both unto God in one body.
  - **[Colossians 2:14-17](/bible/colossians/2#v14)**
    > <sup>[14](/bible/colossians/2#v14)</sup> Blotting out the handwriting of ordinances that was against us, which was contrary to us, and took it out of the way, nailing it to his cross;
    >
    > <sup>[15](/bible/colossians/2#v15)</sup> And having spoiled principalities and powers, he made a shew of them openly, triumphing over them in it.
    >
    > <sup>[16](/bible/colossians/2#v16)</sup> Let no man therefore judge you in meat, or in drink, or in respect of an holyday, or of the new moon, or of the sabbath days:
    >
    > <sup>[17](/bible/colossians/2#v17)</sup> Which are a shadow of things to come; but the body is of Christ.

    Blotting out the handwriting of ordinances that was against us, nailing it to his cross; let no man therefore judge you in meat, or in drink, or of an holyday, or of the new moon, or of the sabbath days: which are a shadow of things to come; but the body is of Christ.
  - **[Hebrews 10:1](/bible/hebrews/10#v1)**
    > <sup>[1](/bible/hebrews/10#v1)</sup> For the law having a shadow of good things to come, and not the very image of the things, can never with those sacrifices which they offered year by year continually make the comers thereunto perfect.

    The law having a shadow of good things to come can never with those sacrifices year by year make the comers thereunto perfect; that is how it was contrary to us.
